increment_paragraph: **CG10-INDIRECT-ACCESS-SOLE-RESIDUALS round 3** (USER DECISION 2026-11-20, "Also, we always blocked indirect-memory access so we must proceed to jump on it." and "Also, we need to proceed other types of indirect memory accesses."; gateway rules 67 and 68, rule 12h amended; Lean `QCore.SiblingBorrowedCalls`, `QCore.PointerTypedefMember`, `QCore.CastActualPlace`; [report](../../reports/cg10-indirect-access-sole-residuals-r3/README.md)). Census of `indirect memory access is outside the resource projection` on the opt-in `current --monkey-linked` run over Fluent Bit 046accf6 at `f916d3007` (inputs prepared on this host; 180 of 180 analysed texts rebuilt sha256-exact; AG1's AST census and eight parallel census-feature selection runs, since census streams force one job): 1,139/2/3,656/7, 2,198 Unknown rows carrying the refusal, 242 by it alone; tables by sub-shape (sole) and by premise and gate site (all rows) with owners. Rule 67 lifts rule 14a's recorded one-call limit for sibling calls each with a `None`-result, all-`Borrowed` contract (each lowered alone in source order; any order C takes leaves every read decided alike, the releasing sibling the counterexample); a nested call stays refused. Rule 68 reads a member declared through an agreeing pointer typedef (`cfl_sds_t name;`) in the single-pointer and borrowable member classes of its `char *` spelling (C11 6.7.8p3). Rule 12h's hook H-U also removes an identity-preserving view of a member place at a call actual (the place hook H-U0 already reads); the return position has no H-U placement. Measured on the opt-in route (base `2f832bda` vs tip `cdcbf730`): 1,139/2/3,656/7 -> 1,140/2/3,655/7, one move `get_stream_path` Unknown -> Safe (rule 67, predicted; on `strlen`'s declared assumption), no Safe -> non-Safe move, no new Unsafe; 55 rows change leaves, access leaves 9,186 -> 9,149, access rows 2,198 -> 2,190, access-alone 242 -> 240; rule 68 re-attributes 14 cmetrics/ctraces rows and removes 35 rows' unresolved-identity leaves. Every remaining class above three rows alone is a design refusal (rules 5k, 10v, 10w), a decision class (1: embedded lists 23, `retained_by` 13; 3), a contract question or MEMBER-EFFECT-STORES, except the return-position cast view (5, CG10-CAST-VIEW-RETURN-POSITION) and the callee-mode sub-object addresses (12). Pinned-route parity not run on this host (no inputs): corpus predicted `get_stream_path` Unknown -> Safe, system and slice none. At integration (integrate/r41) the user decided round 3's decision class 1 questions 1 and 2 (2026-11-20: "Read embedded lists as borrowed container operations"; "Read it as retention, option 1 with creating the relevant proof(s)."), registered as CG10-EMBEDDED-LIST-BORROWED-CONTAINER and CG10-MEMBER-STORE-RETAINED-BY.

ledger.title: A pointer view of a member at an actual of a returned call, or at a statement a Clang-matched reading decides, stays refused (5 sole rows)
ledger.text: Round 3 amended rule 12h's hook H-U to remove an identity-preserving view of a member-chain place at a call actual (`int n = f((const char *)a->name);`). It does not reach `return f((T *)p->m, ...)`: the return position has no H-U placement (a route-map row; adding one is a semantic change with its own identity run), and the uncast spelling matches no Clang node, so a Clang-matched reading (rule 14a's typed member destination `a->n = f((T *)p->m)`) is not reached either. A typed reading at W44's actual (`StatementIndex::argument`) reads the cast but W44 then re-classifies the statement lexically, which does not parse a cast actual. Sole rows on the opt-in route: print_string (cJSON), pb_dec_bool, pb_enc_fixed_length_bytes (nanopb), LZ4F_localSaveDict (an LZ4 union pointer type), sort_by_map_elem_val_toppar_list_cnt (also two pointer declarations from member reads). DISCHARGE: a return-position placement of the H-U removal (route map amended) or a cast-transparent W44 re-classification, with Lean parity and a measurement.

ledger.title: An embedded list's address handed to a list helper is read as a borrowed container operation (USER DECISION 2026-11-20; 23 sole rows)
ledger.text: USER DECISION 2026-11-20 on round 3's decision class 1 question 1, "Read embedded lists as borrowed container operations": a list helper handed the address of a list embedded in a record the body does not own (`rd_list_add(&c->config, e)`, `rd_list_destroy(&conf->interceptors.on_new)`, `pack_static_labels`) is read as a borrowed operation on the container: the body takes no custody of the record or the list, and the list's elements stay the container's. The decision does not decide soundness: a helper that releases or transfers elements (a destroy, a free-elements, a move-in of an owned pointer) still carries that effect on the container's elements and must be discharged by the helper's contract, never read as a no-op; an unstated helper effect stays Unknown (fail-closed). 23 functions on the opt-in route at round 3's tip (Fluent Bit 046accf6) are blocked by this class alone. Rule 46 (container custody) is not superseded; the reading states what it needs from it. DISCHARGE: a gateway reading (rule id, Lean parity) of an embedded-list address at a list helper's actual as Borrowed under the helper's declared mode, with the releasing helpers' element effects carried, a prediction committed before implementation, and an opt-in measurement with no Safe to non-Safe move.

ledger.title: A formal's or local's pointer stored into a member is read as a retention, retained_by, with Lean proofs (USER DECISION 2026-11-20; 13 sole rows)
ledger.text: USER DECISION 2026-11-20 on round 3's decision class 1 question 2, "Read it as retention, option 1 with creating the relevant proof(s).": a formal's or local's pointer stored into a member (`pmi->member = member`, `cio_set_log_callback`) is read as `retained_by(<member place>)`. The body takes no custody of the pointer. Callers inherit the obligation not to release it while the holder keeps it, and that the holder does not outlive it. A caller that cannot discharge this stays Unknown (fail-closed). Function pointers carry no lifetime and may form their own subclass. 13 functions on the opt-in route at round 3's tip (Fluent Bit 046accf6) are blocked by this class alone, 19 mention it. Rule 10v's missing owner premise (Q36) is addressed, not bypassed. DISCHARGE: a gateway reading (rule id, Lean definitions and theorems for the retention obligation, its caller discharge, and a counterexample where the caller releases the retained pointer), a prediction committed before implementation, and an opt-in measurement with no Safe to non-Safe move.
